name: Purpose and audience
excellent: A one-line title states exactly what question the diagram answers; detail fits the intended audience.
partial: Purpose is guessable but mixes audiences.

name: Abstraction consistency
excellent: Boxes use the same level; separate linked views provide zoom-ins.
partial: Mostly consistent with a few stray abstractions.
zero: Infrastructure, code, teams and concepts are jumbled.

name: Completeness vs. focus
excellent: Everything needed to answer the question, nothing else; omissions deliberate and noted.
zero: Critical missing components or buried purpose.

name: Relationships and data flow
excellent: Directed arrows have one meaning, labels say what flows; sync/async and ordering are clear where relevant.

name: Boundaries and grouping
excellent: Trust/network/ownership/deployment containers show internal/external and managed/self-hosted clearly.

name: Visual clarity and layout
excellent: Dominant direction, few crossings, aligned spacing, proximity and readable at the actual viewing size.

name: Notation and legend
excellent: Consistent meaningful shapes/colors/styles, legend for non-obvious conventions, accessible non-color signals, real names.

name: Failure modes and non-functional insight
excellent: Relevant failure points, queues/retries/caches/scaling/state/ownership/external dependencies are explicit.
zero: No sense of behavior under load/failure.

name: Accuracy and freshness
excellent: Matches running system, recently verified, date/version/owner, names match code and dashboards.
partial: Mostly right but unverified or undated.

name: Standalone comprehension
excellent: A new person explains the system correctly in two minutes without the author.
partial: Needs a verbal walkthrough to avoid misreading.
